chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Durost, on the authority of Abil Asbaq that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The body is based on four things: the spirit, the mind; the blood and the self. Once the spirit departs the body, the mind shall follow it. Once the spirit sees something, it will be saved by the mind and maintained by the blood and the self.

key_terms.الرُّوحِ: Spirit or soul, the vital principle
key_terms.وَالنَّفْسِ: The self or soul, often referring to the lower self or life force
key_terms.وَالْعَقْلِ: The intellect or mind, responsible for preservation and reasoning

ai.seo_question: What are the four components that sustain the human body according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam Ali (AS) detailing the four pillars of bodily sustenance: *ruh* (spirit), *aql* (intellect), *dam* (blood), and *nafs* (self). This hadith highlights the hierarchical interdependence of these elements, where the intellect acts as the guardian of the spirit's perceptions, a concept central to Shia anthropological thought. It underscores the physical and metaphysical unity of the human being, linking biological existence with cognitive and spiritual faculties.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-61 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Durost, on the authority of Abil Asbaq that Aba Abdillah (as) said, “

The body is based on four things: the spirit, the mind; the blood and the self. Once the spirit departs the body, the mind shall follow it. Once the spirit sees something, it will be saved by the mind and maintained by the blood and the self.”
